70	`internal/oci/oci.go` — an OCI **registry** HTTP client: list tags,
71	download and extract a tar.gz (a repository template is one — `templates.md`). It speaks the distribution spec over `net/http`
72	and never shells out, so it is engine-agnostic and podman changed nothing in it.
73	
74	**Typed status errors and context variants (DEVDESK-298, IS-18).** A registry,
75	token endpoint or registry manager's management API answering with a
76	non-success status returns `*oci.StatusError{Code, Source, Challenge}`; read it
77	with `errors.As`. `Source` is `SourceRegistry` (the v2 API), `SourceToken` (the
78	Bearer token endpoint) or `SourceManagementAPI` (a manager's own REST API, today
79	Nexus `/service/rest`, DEVDESK-509). `Challenge` is the `Www-Authenticate`
80	header of a 401 whose challenge is not Bearer. `Error()` keeps the three
81	historical messages to the character (`registry returned 404`,
82	`token endpoint returned 403`, `unexpected auth challenge: ...`), so nothing on
83	screen or in a log changed for them. The management API message is
84	`management API returned N`: the code only, never the status line, the body, a
85	header or the URL. It replaces the Nexus client's former `HTTP N`.
86	Failures that are not a status (unreadable body, missing realm, no token
87	field) stay plain errors and do not match `errors.As`.
88	
89	`oci.ManifestDigest` (the `HEAD` on a manifest) is typed too (DEVDESK-631): a
90	non-200 answer returns `fmt.Errorf("%w for %s:%s", &StatusError{Code, Source:
91	SourceRegistry}, repo, tag)`, so `errors.As` finds the `*StatusError` and the
92	text stays `registry returned 404 for repo:tag` to the byte. A 200 without a
93	`Docker-Content-Digest` header stays a plain error (`registry gave no digest for
94	repo:tag`). Its callers (`imageupdate`, the signature stage of `scan`) only log
95	the error and mark the reference failed; none reads the text.
96	
97	A 404 whose body says the proxy's upstream is blocked is marked (DEVDESK-632):
98	`registryStatusError(resp)` (`internal/oci/status_body.go`) builds the
99	`*StatusError` of every non-200 registry answer (tags, catalog, `ManifestDigest`)
100	and, for a 404 only, reads at most 4 KiB of the body (`maxStatusBody`, a
101	hypothesis like `maxNexusErrorBody`). When the body is JSON and the `message` of
102	the first `errors[]` entry starts with `Remote Auto Blocked` (exact, case
103	sensitive, no leading space), `UpstreamBlocked()` is true. A missing, empty,
104	plain-text, longer or cut body, another message, another status (502,
105	403) leaves it false. A body read that ends on a deadline (the client's 15 s
106	delay, the caller's context) is no answer: `registryStatusError` returns the
107	`*NoAnswerError` (verdict `failed`, `no answer within N s`) instead of a plain
108	404; any other read failure (a truncated body, an unexpected EOF) keeps the plain,
109	unmarked 404. `ManifestDigest` is a `HEAD`, which has no body: a "Remote Auto
110	Blocked" 404 on a manifest can never be marked `UpstreamBlocked()` and stays a
111	plain 404 (`refused`). The body never reaches the error: `Error()` is `registry
112	returned 404: the proxy's upstream is temporarily blocked, try again later`, with
113	no date and no duration. `imagesearch.Classify` ranks it `failed` (temporary),
114	not `refused`; the tags footer says `Could not load tags: the proxy's upstream
115	is temporarily blocked` (`registryFailureReason`) and the journal line carries
116	`temporarily blocked`. Every other 404 stays `refused` with `registry returned
117	404`.
118	
119	The unexported `unexpectedChallenge` field is a deviation from the plan, which
120	had only `Code`, `Source` and `Challenge`: with those three, a 401 with a
121	non-Bearer challenge and a 401 returned by the registry after a token exchange
122	both read `Source == SourceRegistry`, `Code == 401`, and `Error()` could not
123	give each its own message. The flag tells them apart without widening the
124	exported surface.
125	
126	`ListRegistryTagsContext` and the `...Context` variants of `registryGET`,
127	`registryDo`, `doRequest` and `exchangeBearerToken` take a `context.Context`
128	(the token endpoint request included) and check `ctx.Err()` at the head of
129	every page. The old names delegate with `context.Background()`, signatures
130	unchanged. A deadline or a cancel reaches the caller as an error that
131	satisfies `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` or `context.Canceled`,
132	and never as a `StatusError`.
133	
134	**The abandon after 15 s is typed (DEVDESK-633).** `oci.RequestTimeout` (15 s,
135	unchanged) is the delay of `registryHTTPClient` and the value of
136	`imageSearchDeadline`. A registry that does not answer in time ends the request
137	with a `*oci.NoAnswerError`, whose text is exactly `no answer within N s`, N read
138	from the constant (no `15` literal outside the tests). It wraps only
139	`context.DeadlineExceeded` (`Unwrap`), so `errors.Is` still finds a deadline,
140	while the URL, userinfo, host, `/v2/` path and query never come back in the
141	message. It is applied to the errors of `doRequestContext`, of the token
142	endpoint's `Do` and `readToken`, and of the body reads of `registryGETContext` and
143	`registryGETBoundedContext` (so tags, catalog, catalog under a prefix, the
144	manifest digest and the token exchange are covered). `context.Canceled` is not
145	touched, and a 502 received in time stays a `*StatusError{502}`, `failed`, with no
146	"no answer". `registryFailureReason` returns the error's own text, so the footer
147	(Error) says `Image search on <alias>: no answer within 15 s` and `Could not load
148	tags: no answer within 15 s`, and the journal reads `ERROR [oci_resources] image
149	search on <alias>: no answer within 15 s`. **Limit:** the client's own delay and the
150	context's deadline are still one case: both give the same error and the same text,
151	and `imagesearch.Classify` (DEVDESK-303, IS-12) puts it in the `failed` verdict.
152	Only a delay that satisfies `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` becomes a
153	`NoAnswerError`: a transport-level "TLS handshake timeout" keeps its own text. The
154	Docker Hub client of `internal/imagesearch/hub.go` keeps its own 15 s delay,
155	untyped (out of scope).
156	
157	**Credentials stay on their origin (DEVDESK-410).** Four guards keep the Basic
158	credentials and the Bearer token from leaving the registry they were meant for:
159	
160	- **The tag list never follows a `Link: rel="next"` to another origin.**
161	  `ListRegistryTagsContext` checks each `next` with `sameOrigin` (the catalog
162	  walker's guard) before the next request. A foreign `next` is an error that
163	  wraps `ErrTagsNextOffOrigin` (test it with `errors.Is`) and names the
164	  destination host only. No partial list is returned: a short list could pass
165	  for the whole one, and `imageupdate` and the security remediation would read
166	  a false "up to date". The catalog walker behaves otherwise: it returns
167	  `truncated=true` with the names already read, and no error.
168	- **`registryHTTPClient` has a `CheckRedirect`, `RefuseOffOriginRedirect`**
169	  (`internal/oci/guard.go`, exported since DEVDESK-412). A
170	  redirect is refused when its scheme, host or port differ from the first
171	  request of the chain (`via[0]`, not only the previous hop), so a chain that
172	  leaves the origin and comes back is refused too. The error reads
173	  `refusing redirect to another origin (<host>)` and wraps
174	  `ErrOffOriginRedirect` (`errors.Is`). It holds neither the target URL, nor
175	  its path or query: `StripRedirectTarget` strips the `*url.Error` that carries
176	  them, so a signed URL reaches neither the footer nor the logs. The limit of
177	  10 redirects (`MaxRedirects`, the `net/http` default) is kept; past it the
178	  error wraps `ErrTooManyRedirects` (`stopped after 10 redirects`) and no
179	  longer carries the last target URL either. It applies to everything that uses
180	  the client: tags, catalog and the token endpoint.
181	- **The token endpoint's answer is capped at 1 MiB** (`maxTokenResponse`). A
182	  larger body is an error (`token response over 1048576 bytes`), not a silent
183	  cut.
184	- **A Bearer realm on another origin gets no credentials (DEVDESK-629,
185	  D168).** `exchangeBearerTokenContext` calls `checkRealmOrigin`
186	  (`internal/oci/realm.go`) right after `checkTokenRealm`: when credentials
187	  are configured (username and password both set, the condition under which
188	  Basic is sent) and the realm's scheme, host or port differ from the request
189	  that received the challenge, the exchange stops before any request to the
190	  realm with an error wrapping `ErrTokenRealmOffOrigin`
191	  (`token realm on another host (<host>)`, `errors.Is`), naming the realm's host
192	  only and not a `StatusError`. Without credentials the anonymous token request
193	  goes out as before. The comparison is `sameOrigin`'s, exact: `host` and
194	  `host:443` are two origins (H2). Two exceptions, frozen in `realmExceptions`
195	  (a test pins the list), one way, https on both sides, host exact with no
196	  port: Docker Hub (`registry-1.docker.io` to `auth.docker.io`) and GitLab.com
197	  (`registry.gitlab.com` to `gitlab.com`). A self-hosted GitLab registry whose
198	  realm is on the GitLab host is refused. The refusal shows at the footer, level
199	  Error, as `token realm on another host`, in the three interactive flows of the
200	  registry browser: tags opened from the search (`Could not load tags: token
201	  realm on another host`), tags opened from the form (silent before, this one
202	  failure only, H1) and image search (`Image search on <alias>: token realm on
203	  another host`), through `registryFailureReason`
204	  (`internal/ui/oci_resources/registry_failure.go`); the search verdict is
205	  `failed`. The realm's host stays in the journal. The other callers
206	  (`imageupdate`, signature, remediation) have no footer.
207	
208	**Behavior change.** Some redirects that were followed are now refused: `http`
209	to `https` on the same host, `host` to `host:443`, and a host written with a
210	different case. The comparison is on the exact scheme and `host:port`, and the
211	guard refuses when in doubt.
212	
213	**Behavior change (DEVDESK-629).** A registry configured with credentials whose
214	Bearer realm is on another origin (other than the two exceptions above) used to
215	receive them as Basic at its token endpoint; it now fails with
216	`token realm on another host`. Without credentials nothing changes.
217	
218	**The other registry clients (DEVDESK-412).** The same two guards, plus a few
219	more, cover the clients DEVDESK-410 left out. The shared code is
220	`internal/oci/guard.go`, which `internal/registrymgr` imports (`internal/oci`
221	imports nothing from `internal/`).
222	
223	- **`guard.go`** exports `MaxRedirects`, `ErrOffOriginRedirect`,
224	  `ErrTooManyRedirects`, `RefuseOffOriginRedirect` and `StripRedirectTarget`
225	  (which also unwraps the unexported `errInsecureRedirect` and the blob's local
226	  refusal), and two helpers. `ReadAllLimited(r, limit)` accepts `limit` bytes
227	  and fails with an error wrapping `ErrBodyTooLarge` (`response body over
228	  <limit> bytes`) on the next one: never a silent cut. `RedactURL(raw)` masks
229	  the password of a URL's userinfo (`xxxxx`) and returns `<invalid URL>` for

286	  so the host name stays readable; an unreadable address gives `<invalid URL>`.
287	  `browser_bridge.go` (tags and tag-meta logs) and the login and logout logs of
288	  `registries.go` and `commands.go` use it. In `internal/template/fetch.go`,
289	  `redactGitURL` masks the source URL in `fetching ...` for `http(s)` URLs (the
290	  scp form `git@host:path` is kept as written); it is being extended to mask a
291	  token written as the user name of an `http(s)` URL as well. A password written
292	  in a registry URL (`https://alice:...@host`) reaches neither the footer nor
293	  `log.Printf`.
294	- **The Nexus detector** (`internal/registrymgr/nexus.go`) has the same origin
295	  guard (`nexusHTTPClient.CheckRedirect = oci.RefuseOffOriginRedirect`, 8 s
296	  timeout unchanged) and reads each reply through
297	  `oci.ReadAllLimited(..., maxNexusResponse)`, 1 MiB. The cap is a hypothesis,
298	  not measured. The anonymous retry of the group members still happens on any
299	  error but a refused off-origin redirect (see `registries.md`); the first
300	  attempt decides the outcome, the retry only changes it by succeeding.
301	  `fetchGroupMembers` no longer swallows its errors (DEVDESK-510): a
302	  `StatusError` from the management API with 401 or 403, or the 404 Nexus
303	  answers a pull account (DEVDESK-578), becomes
304	  `*registrymgr.MembersRefusedError` (`errors.Is(err, ErrMembersRefused)`,
305	  `Group`, `Status`, `Anonymous`; its text holds the group and the status,
306	  never a URL or a body; for the 404, `Cause` is the plain
307	  `*oci.StatusError`), any other error is returned as it is. `nexusGET` reads
308	  the body of a 404 only, up to 4 KiB (`maxNexusErrorBody`, a hypothesis: the
309	  measured body is about 50 bytes), and only to check that its JSON `message`
310	  is `Repository not found`; the body never reaches an error or a log. A 404
311	  with any other body, or a longer one, stays a plain status error. A reply
312	  without a `group.memberNames` key (empty body, `null`, `{}`) is an error;
313	  `memberNames: []` is a group with no member, a non-nil empty list. The format
314	  segment of the path is escaped (`url.PathEscape`). A non-200
315	  status is `*oci.StatusError{Source: oci.SourceManagementAPI}`
316	  (`management API returned 401`). A context error (cancel, deadline) is never
317	  a `StatusError`: when the context is done, a body cut mid-read reports the
318	  context's own error. A 200 reply that is not a repository document (empty or
319	  whitespace-only body, JSON without a `type` such as `{}` or `null`, invalid
320	  JSON) is an error wrapping `errEmptyReply`, `errNoRepositoryType` or the
321	  `encoding/json` error, never "not a group": the caller does not cache it
322	  (D23), so the members last known stay.
323	- **Each member is typed by one more GET (DEVDESK-636).** After the member names
324	  are known (either endpoint), `memberTypes` asks
325	  `/service/rest/v1/repositories/<member>` for each one (the name through
326	  `url.PathEscape`, `nexusHTTPClient`, the group's credentials or none, at most
327	  `maxTypedMembers` = 32 members and `typeLookupWorkers` = 8 at once) and keeps
328	  `type` when it is `hosted`, `proxy` or `group`. A failure (status, deadline,
329	  redirect refused, invalid JSON, `{}`, `null`, any other value) leaves the
330	  member's `GroupMember.Type` empty (unknown), is logged at INFO with the server
331	  values quoted (`%q`, an unrecognized `type` cut to 64 characters first), and
332	  never fails the discovery or changes the list. No lookup is started once the
333	  context is done (the loop checks `ctx.Err()` and its wait for a free slot
334	  listens to `ctx`); the members not reached stay unknown. A
335	  group refused or not a group asks for no type. Cost: up to 32 more requests per
336	  `ctrl+r` on a Nexus group, none at start-up or at search time. The measured
337	  generic answers (`rest-repositories-docker-{hosted,proxy}--*`) carry `type`
338	  for all three identities.
339	- **Docker Hub tag dates** (`fetchDockerHubTagsMeta`, `commands.go`) read the
340	  page through `oci.ReadAllLimited(..., maxHubTagsMetaResponse)`, 4 MiB.
341	  Measured on 2026-11-16 with `page_size=100`: 530,629 bytes for
342	  `library/postgres` (the largest), 443,387 for `library/python`, 259,560 for
343	  `library/node`; the cap is about 7.9 times the largest. A page over it is an
344	  error wrapping `ErrBodyTooLarge` and no dates are returned (no partial map).
345	  `ociHTTPClient` is unchanged (15 s timeout, anonymous call, no credentials).
346	
347	**Behavior change (DEVDESK-412).** A Bearer realm in `http://` behind an
348	`https` registry is refused, and so is a realm with another scheme. A template
349	blob redirected from `https` to `http`, or to a loopback or link-local address
350	from a registry that is not local, is refused. A registry that serves its
351	layers with a digest other than `sha256` can no longer be used as an OCI
352	template source. A Nexus URL that redirects to another origin gives no members
353	(the `http` to `https` redirect of the same host included: enter the URL in
354	`https`).
355	
356	**Residual risks.** The accepted ones (private networks not filtered, local
357	registry named by an alias, proxy behavior, CPU before the digest check, sha256
358	only, Nexus limits, and the rest) are listed in D156 in `docs/backlog.md`.
359	
360	**Catalog walk (DEVDESK-306, IS-03).** `ListCatalogContext(ctx, apiURL,
361	username, password, maxPages, pageSize)` returns `(names, truncated, err)`. It
362	asks `<apiURL>/v2/_catalog?n=<pageSize>` and follows `Link: rel="next"` for at
363	most `maxPages` pages (non-positive limits are an error). `truncated` is true
364	when names were left: the page cap was reached with a `next` link, more than
365	`maxPages*pageSize` names came back (the list is cut to that), or the `next`
366	link points to another origin. A name already returned is skipped silently
367	(first appearance order kept; a Nexus group repeats names across pages, the
368	measured `n=2` walk, DEVDESK-634), and the `maxPages*pageSize` cap counts
369	distinct names. Each page body is capped at 1 MiB; a larger
370	page is an error, not a silent cut. A non-200 answer is a `*StatusError`.
371	Authentication is the tags' flow: Basic, then Bearer on a challenge, the token
372	kept across pages.
373	
374	- **`next` is followed only to the same origin.** `sameOrigin` compares scheme
375	  and host strictly (`host` and `host:443` differ), so a registry cannot make
376	  the walk send the Basic credentials or the token elsewhere. A foreign or
377	  differently written `next` ends the walk as `truncated`, with no error.
378	- **HTTP 3xx redirects are hardened too** (DEVDESK-410): the walk goes through
379	  `registryHTTPClient`, whose `CheckRedirect` refuses a redirect to another
380	  origin (see "Credentials stay on their origin" above).
381	- **Under a prefix, `next` must also stay on the member's catalog path.** A
382	  non-empty prefix follows a `next` only when its escaped path is exactly
383	  `/v2/<prefix>/_catalog` (same origin already checked); a link to
384	  `/v2/_catalog` or to another repository would attach the names of another
385	  catalog to the prefix, so it ends the walk as `truncated`, unfollowed. With
386	  an empty prefix any same-origin path is followed, as before.
387	
388	**Catalog under a prefix (DEVDESK-579, NX-12).** `ListCatalogUnderContext(ctx,
389	apiURL, prefix, username, password, maxPages, pageSize)` is the same walk on
390	`/v2/<prefix>/_catalog`, the catalog of one Nexus group member; `ListCatalogContext`
391	is it with an empty prefix, and the two rules above apply to it unchanged. Names
392	come back as the server sent them, without the prefix (the caller rebuilds
393	`<prefix>/<name>`). Each prefix segment goes through `url.PathEscape`, so a
394	space, `%`, `?`, `#` or an already-encoded `%2F` stays one segment on the wire.
395	A prefix is refused before any request, with an error that gives the rule and
396	never carries the prefix or a credential, when it has an empty segment (leading,
397	trailing or doubled `/`), a `.` segment, any `..` (read literally, `a..b` too),
398	a backslash, a segment of spaces only, a control character (NUL included), a
399	segment over 255 bytes or a prefix over 1024 bytes. The blank segment, the
400	control characters and the length bounds are a choice: no repository name holds
401	them. Under a prefix, `next` is also held to the member's catalog path (last
402	bullet above).
403	
404	## Image search — `internal/imagesearch` (DEVDESK-298, IS-18)
405	
406	Pure Go, no UI. Types and one interface; two adapters, `HubSearcher` (IS-02)
407	and `CatalogSearcher` (IS-03); dhi.io is IS-17:
408	
409	- `Target`: one registry to search (`EntryKey`, `Alias`, `RegistryURL`,
410	  `APIURL`, `RepoPrefix`, `Username`, `Password`; the credentials are empty for
411	  an anonymous entry, D12).
412	- `Query{Text, Limit}`: `Limit` 0 is the adapter's default.
413	- `Image`: one result (`EntryKey`, `Name`, `Repo`, `Description`, `Stars`,
414	  `HasStars`, `Official`). `Repo` is the final path, with the prefix and
415	  `library/` applied once (D39).
416	- `Searcher.Search(ctx, Target, Query) (images, partial, err)`, and
417	  `SearcherFunc`, the function adapter.
418	- `HubSearcher` (DEVDESK-301, IS-02, `hub.go`): anonymous, one GET on
419	  `https://index.docker.io/v1/search` (the endpoint `docker search` uses, not a
420	  public Hub contract), one page of at most `HubLimit` (50) results, no
421	  credentials (Target's are ignored), no redirects, 15 s client timeout, body
422	  capped at 1 MiB. A non-200 answer is an `*oci.StatusError`. A result without
423	  `star_count` keeps `HasStars` false (the Stars cell stays empty, never 0).
424	  Names are validated against a regex (`hubComponent`: lowercase alphanumerics
425	  joined by `.`, `_`, `__` or runs of `-`, as in the OCI distribution spec); a
426	  name that fails is dropped (`-rm`, `--help`, uppercase, `a//b`, a leading or
427	  trailing separator). A description is sanitised: escape sequences, control
428	  characters and Unicode format characters (category Cf: bidi overrides,
429	  zero-width, BOM) are removed. Privacy: the text the user typed is sent to
430	  Docker Hub as soon as a Hub entry is checked.
431	- `ByRegistry(hub, other)` (`route.go`): a target whose host is exactly `dhi.io`
432	  (DEVDESK-303, `isDHI`: case, scheme, port and path ignored; `registry.dhi.io`
433	  and `notdhi.io` are not dhi.io) is refused first, with `ErrUnsupported` and no
434	  request to either searcher, since dhi.io has no documented catalogue API
435	  (IS-17). Otherwise a target for which `oci.IsDockerHub(RegistryURL)` is true
436	  goes to `hub`, any other to `other`. A nil searcher answers `ErrUnsupported`
437	  with no request at all. Production uses
438	  `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})`: Hub goes to the Hub search,
439	  every other registry to its catalog. `isDHI` parses the URL (`url.Parse`, with
440	  `https://` added when there is no scheme) and compares `Hostname()`, so
441	  userinfo (`dhi.io@evil.example`), a trailing dot and a port cannot fool it.
442	- `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306, IS-03, `catalog.go`): searches a private
443	  registry by walking `/v2/_catalog` through `oci.ListCatalogContext` (or, for a
444	  Nexus member, `/v2/<prefix>/_catalog`, see "Catalog under a prefix" below) and
445	  filtering **client-side**: the text the user typed is never sent to the
446	  registry. Steps, in order:
447	  1. The query is trimmed; fewer than `CatalogMinQueryRunes` (2) runes returns
448	     `ErrQueryTooShort` with **no request**.
449	  2. The walk: `CatalogPageSize` (1000) names per page, at most
450	     `CatalogMaxPages` (10) pages, so at most 10 000 names. A cut walk sets
451	     `truncated`. An error from the walk (status, deadline, unreadable page)
452	     is returned as is, with no row.
453	  3. Guard R1 (before the filter), **root catalog only**: when the target has a `RepoPrefix`, only the
454	     names that start with `<prefix>/` are candidates. If the walk is complete and
455	     no name carries the prefix, the answer is `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` (the
456	     cause names the prefix); this protects against a catalog that does not
457	     list names the way the entry reaches them (Nexus, IS-16) and would
458	     otherwise read as a false "no result". If the walk is truncated, the
459	     prefix may be on a page not read: the answer is no result with
460	     `partial` set, not an error. A target with `CatalogUnderPrefix` skips this
461	     step (see below).
462	  4. Filter: case-insensitive substring match on the part **after** the prefix.
463	     `Image.Name` is that part, `Image.Repo` the full catalog name.
464	  5. Only valid names are kept (`validRepoPath`, `names.go`: every
465	     `/`-separated component follows the distribution-spec grammar, as for Hub);
466	     others are dropped.
467	  6. Order by `MatchTier`, then name, then `Repo`; at most `CatalogMaxRows`
468	     (100) rows (`Query.Limit` can only lower that). Rows cut by the limit set
469	     `partial`, as does a truncated walk.
470	
471	  `MatchTier` (ranks 0 to 4, see the order below) now lives in `imagesearch`
472	  (`names.go`) so the searcher and the table share one ranking;
473	  `oci_resources.matchTier` delegates to it. The 15 s per-registry deadline
474	  (`imageSearchDeadline`, below) covers the whole walk; hitting it is a
475	  `failed` verdict with no row. `CatalogSearcher.List` replaces
476	  `oci.ListCatalogContext` in tests. Walks per search
477	  (DEVDESK-311, IS-07, `walks.go`): `WithSharedWalks(ctx)` puts a memo on the
478	  batch context and `CatalogSearcher` goes through `walkCatalog`, so a search
479	  queries `/v2/_catalog` once per API URL and identity. Without the memo
480	  (any other caller) every call walks on its own.
481	  - Key: the exact API URL (trailing slash ignored), the catalog prefix
482	    (`catalogPrefix`, empty for the root catalog; DEVDESK-579) and the identity, an
483	    HMAC-SHA256 of username and password under a random per-batch key: no
484	    secret is held in clear and the key prints no userinfo. Two identities
485	    never share a walk, because Harbor, Artifactory and GitLab filter the
486	    catalog per account. A `credentials` entry with no effective secret shares
487	    the walk of an anonymous entry. A member on another port or subdomain has
488	    another API URL and is not grouped. Two Nexus members of one host read two
489	    different catalogs, so they have two keys and two walks: D140 no longer
490	    merges them (D167 amends it). Entries on the root catalog still share one
491	    walk per API URL and identity.
492	  - Leader and followers: the first call for a key walks, the others wait (or
493	    return on their own context). It is a memo, not a singleflight: the key is
494	    kept after the walk, so a member arriving later reuses the result, and it
495	    dies with the batch (no cache between two searches).
496	  - A shared failure (a 503, say) is the same error for every member, so the
497	    same verdict (`failed` or `refused`), one message per entry. A result
498	    caused by the leader's own context ending is not memoized: followers
499	    already waiting on that flight receive the leader's context error (verdict
500	    `failed`), and only members arriving afterwards walk again. A
501	    panic in the leader gives followers a sentinel error (`errWalkAborted`),
502	    never an empty catalog.
503	  - `repo_prefix` filtering, `partial`, `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` and the
504	    `May omit images` mention stay computed per member.
505	  - Members of one Nexus host do **not** answer on the same `/v2/_catalog`
506	    (measured, Nexus 3.98.1-01): each answers on its own path catalog, which is why
507	    the key carries the prefix. For other registries on one host the assumption
508	    stays unverified.
509	  A catalog may be disabled or filtered to the account's rights (Harbor,
510	  Artifactory, GitLab): the answer is then `refused` or a shortened list.
511	- **`Target.CatalogUnderPrefix` (DEVDESK-579, NX-12).** A Nexus member has no
512	  usable root catalog: `/v2/_catalog` answers 404 on the HTTP port, and on a
513	  group connector it lists the members' names together with no member attribution.
514	  With the flag set, `CatalogSearcher` hands the lister `catalogPrefix = RepoPrefix`
515	  and reads `/v2/<prefix>/_catalog`. Differences from the root catalog:
516	  - Nexus returns names **without** the prefix; `Image.Repo` is rebuilt as
517	    `<prefix>/<name>`.
518	  - No guard R1: every name belongs to the member. An empty catalog is
519	    `no result`, not `refused`.
520	  - A prefix that fails `validRepoPath` is `refused` before any request. That
521	    check refuses uppercase, so a catalog name outside the OCI grammar is
522	    ignored and a member whose repository name has uppercase is refused. Not
523	    measured: whether Nexus serves `/v2/<UpperCaseName>/_catalog`.
524	  - Verdicts: 404, 401, 403 and 405 are `refused`; 5xx, 429 and network errors
525	    are `failed`.
526	  - The walk key holds the prefix (D140 amended, above). No request goes to
527	    `/v2/_catalog` for these targets.
528	  Who sets the flag is the UI's decision: see "Image search and Nexus members"
529	  below. Every other target keeps the root catalog and R1.
530	- **Verdicts (DEVDESK-303, IS-12, `verdict.go`).** `Classify(err, n, partial)`
531	  is a pure function that turns one registry's answer into an `Outcome{Verdict,
532	  Partial, Skipped}`. `Verdict` is one of `VerdictOK` (`ok`), `VerdictNoResult`
533	  (`no result`), `VerdictRefused` (`unsupported or refused`) and
534	  `VerdictFailed` (`failed`); the zero value is not a verdict (`pending`) and
535	  `Classify` never returns it. `Partial` and `Skipped` are marks, not verdicts:
536	  `Partial` with `ok` or `no result` (invariant Q1: a walk cut short that found
537	  nothing is still `no result`, marked `Partial`), never with `refused` or
538	  `failed`, never with `Skipped`; `Skipped` only with `no result`. Rules, first
539	  match wins:
540	  1. no error: `n > 0` is `ok`, `n == 0` is `no result`; `Partial` is kept as
541	     given in both cases;
542	  2. `ErrQueryTooShort` is `no result` with `Skipped`;
543	  3. `ErrUnsupported` or `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` is `refused`;
544	  4. a `*oci.StatusError` is `refused` when `refusedStatus` holds: 401 and 403
545	     from either source, 404 and 405 from `SourceRegistry` only (a 404 from the
546	     token endpoint is a failure), except a 404 marked `UpstreamBlocked()` (a
547	     Nexus proxy whose upstream is blocked, DEVDESK-632), which is `failed`;
548	     any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is `failed`;
549	  5. anything else is `failed`: deadline, cancel, network, unreadable or
550	     oversized body, invalid request.
551	
552	  `ErrQueryTooShort` and `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` are returned by
553	  `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306).
554	
555	## Image updates — `internal/imageupdate` (§3.88)
556	
557	Three tables carry an **Update** column (`internal/ui/updatecol`): oci's Images
558	tab, the containers list, and the Remediation tab of a scan result. It shows an
559	arrow when the image's registry holds something newer, and says what:
560	
561	| Kind | When | Cell |
562	|---|---|---|
563	| `NewPatch` | the tag has ≥ 3 version components and a tag differing only by the last, same variant, is higher (`20.11.1-alpine` → `20.11.4-alpine`) | the arrow and the tag |
564	| `NewBuild` | the digest the tag points to now is none of the local image's digests | the arrow alone (`IconArrowDown`) |
565

745	*Header.* `FormEnter()` returns the label and the lit state of the header's
746	single `enter` entry. The label follows the focus: `Search` on Repository and
747	on the Search button (`Browse tags` without a `Searcher`), `Open tags` on the
748	Open Tags button. `enter` is lit on Repository (Rule 130: it submits there) and
749	on a button, and greyed on a checkbox.
750	
751	*Help.* `registryBrowserHelpBody(searchEnabled)` (`view.go`) depends on the
752	mode (Rule 114): without a `Searcher` it names Browse Tags only; with one it
753	describes Search, Open Tags and the shared selection, and the level 1 sentence.
754	
755	**`defaultImageSearcher` is `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})` in
756	production (DEVDESK-301, IS-02; catalog since DEVDESK-306, IS-03), so level 1
757	and Open Tags are active.** `newRegistryBrowser`
758	copies it into `b.searcher`. Tests do not use it: `TestMain`
759	(`ociresources_test.go`) saves it in `productionImageSearcher` and sets
760	`defaultImageSearcher` to `nil` for the whole suite (no test may reach the real
761	Hub), and tests inject a fake with `withImageSearcher`.
762	`TestProductionWiresTheHubSearcher` reads the saved value. `internal/app`
763	injects nothing: its tests avoid level 1 by typing a name with a `/`.
764	
765	`startImageSearch` runs one `searchImagesCmd` per checked registry, with
766	`targetFor(entry)` (same credentials as the tag flow, `credsFor`). Each command
767	wraps the lot's context in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, imageSearchDeadline)`:
768	`imageSearchDeadline` is 15 s **per registry**, the whole walk included, on top
769	of the 15 s client timeout per request (`imageSearchDeadline = oci.RequestTimeout`,
770	see "The abandon after 15 s is typed" above). A registry's
771	answer arrives as `ImageSearchResultMsg{Gen, EntryKey, Images, Partial, Err}`
772	and `AddImageResults` takes it (false when stale; `pendingSearches` never goes
773	under 0).
774	
775	**Verdicts per registry (DEVDESK-303, IS-12).** `AddImageResults` calls
776	`imagesearch.Classify` in `Update`, never in the `Cmd` (Rule 110), and stores the
777	result in `RegistryBrowser.outcomes`, keyed by `EntryKey`. The map is reset by
778	`startImageSearch`, so it holds one lot only; a registry with no entry is still
779	pending. Only an `ok` verdict appends rows. `Outcome(entryKey)` reads one
780	verdict (false while pending). `Model.RegistryBrowserOutcomes()` returns a copy
781	of the map, or nil when the browser is closed; it is for the tests and for IS-13.
782	
783	**Image search and Nexus members (DEVDESK-579, NX-12).** `targetFor` sets
784	`CatalogUnderPrefix` on two kinds of entry: a plain entry that lists cached
785	content only and has a `repo_prefix` (a `parent:` entry of a `provider: nexus`
786	group), and a discovered member of a Nexus group that has a `repo_prefix`. The two
787	tests are equivalent, because `checkRepoPrefixes` refuses a `repo_prefix` on a
788	group. Any other entry keeps the root catalog and guard R1.
789	
790	`searchUnits` decides what a lot searches. Discovered members **without an
791	address of their own** (same URL and same `repo_prefix` as their group, with the
792	group's slug as `ParentSlug`) are merged into **one** unit, the group, labelled
793	`<alias> (group)` (`groupUnitSuffix`). It is walked once, and its rows name no
794	member: Nexus does not say which member holds a name. By design this bypasses the
795	picker's selection: ticking one bare member searches the whole group, and a row can
796	carry the name of a member that was unticked. A group that was not discovered (a
797	pull account) is searched as itself, with its bare label. The Registry column
798	keeps the whole suffix when it cuts a cell (`datatable.Column.KeepSuffix`, see
799	`ui-components.md`). `lotUnits` holds the units of the current lot until the next
800	image search; `entryFor` falls back on it, so labels, the `→` tags drill of a group
801	row and the `r` filter work on a unit. The `?` help says: `'nx (group)': images
802	found through the group; Nexus does not say which member holds each one.`
803	
804	**Level 1 header summary (DEVDESK-305, IS-13).** `searchHeaderInfo`
805	(`browser_summary.go`, called from `GetHeaderInfo`) says what the lot did, one
806	header line per class, in this order: `Images` (the row count, always), then
807	`Pending` (a count, live lot) or `Interrupted` (names, the lot was abandoned
808	with the left arrow before they answered), `Failed` (red), `Refused`, `Partial`
809	(orange), `May omit images` (orange, DEVDESK-308 IS-14, reworded by DEVDESK-629 F2), `No result` (dim) and `Skipped` (dim, catalog not walked because the
810	query is shorter than `imagesearch.CatalogMinQueryRunes`). A class with nothing
811	to say has no line, so a lot where every registry answered shows only `Images`.
812	`summarizeSearch` (pure) sorts the lot's keys into the classes. A name is the
813	Registry column's label (`entryLabel`: alias, else URL, else key), in form order.
814	`Partial` lists registries cut at a cap, `No result` those that answered with
815	nothing (Skipped excluded). A registry that is both partial and empty appears
816	on both lines, on purpose.
817	
818	`May omit images` lists the registries that may not have listed every image
819	they hold, by their role in a Nexus group (DEVDESK-629, F2; it replaces the
820	`Cached only` line of DEVDESK-308, whose "limited to cached content" reading the
821	measures of NX-04 contradicted). `browserRegistryEntry.role` is a `nexusRole`
822	(group, proxy, hosted, unknown), set once by `buildEntries`: a
823	`provider: nexus` + `kind: group` entry is a group; a discovered member of one
824	takes `memberRole(RegistryGroupMember.Type)` (`hosted`, `proxy`, `group`; any
825	other value, case included, is unknown); a declared entry whose `parent` is the
826	slug of a Nexus group takes the type of the discovered member at its exact
827	`(URL, RepoPrefix)`, and is unknown when none matches or the cache predates the
828	type (H5); a group unit (`groupUnit`) is a group. `isNexusGroupOrMember` (the
829	former `listsCacheOnly`) only drives `catalogUnderPrefix`. The pure rule is
830	`mayOmit(role, outcome)`: a group whatever it answered (it says nothing about
831	what a member it could not reach left out), a proxy only when it `failed` or was
832	`refused`, a hosted repository never, an unknown role never (no mention is better
833	than a false one), and never a `Skipped` outcome. `summarizeSearch` takes a
834	`func(string) nexusRole` and reads it by entry key (`entryRole`, not by slug:
835	members share their group's slug). A group that answered with no result is
836	marked ` (no result)` on that line and is not on `No result`; the mark does not
837	mean the image is absent, only that this registry listed nothing and may have
838	left out what it could not reach, while `No result: quay` means the registry
839	answered and holds nothing that matches. A `failed` or `refused` mention stays on
840	its own line too and carries no mark; a partial registry appears on `Partial` and
841	on `May omit images`. Docker Hub, generic registries and a Nexus outside a group
842	never get the line. `Skipped` and `May omit images` exclude each other (`Skipped`
843	means no catalog entry answered), which keeps the budget below. The search sends
844	no request to the members of a group (F4): the group answers on its own connector,
845	and a member the group could not reach is invisible to DevDesk; the line says it
846	may happen, it cannot say it did. The MCP server is unchanged.
847	The Nexus catalog tests of `internal/imagesearch` (`TestCatalogOnMeasuredNexusAnswers`)
848	replay answers measured on the bench (Nexus 3.98.1-01, NX-03), not hand-written
849	ones: the verdicts `ok`, `No result` and `Refused` (prefix absent from a real
850	catalog) are checked there. `Failed` and the group line are measured since NX-04
851	(DEVDESK-580, PR3): a proxy's catalog lists names it does not hold
852	(`mirror/uncached`) while its upstream answers, and a group on its connector answers
853	`no result` for `mirror` once a member's upstream is cut, which is why `(no result)`
854	does not mean absent.
855	See "Recorded fixtures" in [`nexus-bench.md`](nexus-bench.md).
856	
857	Each name list is fitted by `fitNames` to the room a value has
858	(`shortcut.HeaderValueWidth`), so the `+N` is never lost: all the names, else
859	the first k names then `+N`, else `+N` alone. `Skipped` carries the hint
860	` (type N+ characters)`, which is the first thing dropped when the header is
861	narrow. The summary has a budget of `shortcut.HeaderRows` (7) lines, `Images`
862	included; classes after the sixth are left out (with `May omit images` the seven
863	classes fit only because `Pending`/`Interrupted` and `Skipped`/`May omit images`

70	`internal/oci/oci.go` — an OCI **registry** HTTP client: list tags,
71	download and extract a tar.gz (a repository template is one — `templates.md`). It speaks the distribution spec over `net/http`
72	and never shells out, so it is engine-agnostic and podman changed nothing in it.
73	
74	**Typed status errors and context variants (DEVDESK-298, IS-18).** A registry,
75	token endpoint or registry manager's management API answering with a
76	non-success status returns `*oci.StatusError{Code, Source, Challenge}`; read it
77	with `errors.As`. `Source` is `SourceRegistry` (the v2 API), `SourceToken` (the
78	Bearer token endpoint) or `SourceManagementAPI` (a manager's own REST API, today
79	Nexus `/service/rest`, DEVDESK-509). `Challenge` is the `Www-Authenticate`
80	header of a 401 whose challenge is not Bearer. `Error()` keeps the three
81	historical messages to the character (`registry returned 404`,
82	`token endpoint returned 403`, `unexpected auth challenge: ...`), so nothing on
83	screen or in a log changed for them. The management API message is
84	`management API returned N`: the code only, never the status line, the body, a
85	header or the URL. It replaces the Nexus client's former `HTTP N`.
86	Failures that are not a status (unreadable body, missing realm, no token
87	field) stay plain errors and do not match `errors.As`.
88	
89	`oci.ManifestDigest` (the `HEAD` on a manifest) is typed too (DEVDESK-631): a
90	non-200 answer returns `fmt.Errorf("%w for %s:%s", &StatusError{Code, Source:
91	SourceRegistry}, repo, tag)`, so `errors.As` finds the `*StatusError` and the
92	text stays `registry returned 404 for repo:tag` to the byte. A 200 without a
93	`Docker-Content-Digest` header stays a plain error (`registry gave no digest for
94	repo:tag`). Its callers (`imageupdate`, the signature stage of `scan`) only log
95	the error and mark the reference failed; none reads the text.
96	
97	A 404 whose body says the proxy's upstream is blocked is marked (DEVDESK-632):
98	`registryStatusError(resp)` (`internal/oci/status_body.go`) builds the
99	`*StatusError` of every non-200 registry answer (tags, catalog, `ManifestDigest`)
100	and, for a 404 only, reads at most 4 KiB of the body (`maxStatusBody`, a
101	hypothesis like `maxNexusErrorBody`). When the body is JSON and the `message` of
102	the first `errors[]` entry starts with `Remote Auto Blocked` (exact, case
103	sensitive, no leading space), `UpstreamBlocked()` is true. A missing, empty,
104	plain-text, longer or cut body, another message, another status (502,
105	403) leaves it false. A body read that ends on a deadline (the client's 15 s
106	delay, the caller's context) is no answer: `registryStatusError` returns the
107	`*NoAnswerError` (verdict `failed`, `no answer within N s`) instead of a plain
108	404; any other read failure (a truncated body, an unexpected EOF) keeps the plain,
109	unmarked 404. `ManifestDigest` is a `HEAD`, which has no body: a "Remote Auto
110	Blocked" 404 on a manifest can never be marked `UpstreamBlocked()` and stays a
111	plain 404 (`refused`). The body never reaches the error: `Error()` is `registry
112	returned 404: the proxy's upstream is temporarily blocked, try again later`, with
113	no date and no duration. `imagesearch.Classify` ranks it `failed` (temporary),
114	not `refused`; the tags footer says `Could not load tags: the proxy's upstream
115	is temporarily blocked` (`registryFailureReason`) and the journal line carries
116	`temporarily blocked`. Every other 404 stays `refused` with `registry returned
117	404`.
118	
119	The unexported `unexpectedChallenge` field is a deviation from the plan, which
120	had only `Code`, `Source` and `Challenge`: with those three, a 401 with a
121	non-Bearer challenge and a 401 returned by the registry after a token exchange
122	both read `Source == SourceRegistry`, `Code == 401`, and `Error()` could not
123	give each its own message. The flag tells them apart without widening the
124	exported surface.
125	
126	`ListRegistryTagsContext` and the `...Context` variants of `registryGET`,
127	`registryDo`, `doRequest` and `exchangeBearerToken` take a `context.Context`
128	(the token endpoint request included) and check `ctx.Err()` at the head of
129	every page. The old names delegate with `context.Background()`, signatures
130	unchanged. A deadline or a cancel reaches the caller as an error that
131	satisfies `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` or `context.Canceled`,
132	and never as a `StatusError`.
133	
134	**The abandon after 15 s is typed (DEVDESK-633).** `oci.RequestTimeout` (15 s,
135	unchanged) is the delay of `registryHTTPClient` and the value of
136	`imageSearchDeadline`. A registry that does not answer in time ends the request
137	with a `*oci.NoAnswerError`, whose text is exactly `no answer within N s`, N read
138	from the constant (no `15` literal outside the tests). It wraps only
139	`context.DeadlineExceeded` (`Unwrap`), so `errors.Is` still finds a deadline,
140	while the URL, userinfo, host, `/v2/` path and query never come back in the
141	message. It is applied to the errors of `doRequestContext`, of the token
142	endpoint's `Do` and `readToken`, and of the body reads of `registryGETContext` and
143	`registryGETBoundedContext` (so tags, catalog, catalog under a prefix, the
144	manifest digest and the token exchange are covered). `context.Canceled` is not
145	touched, and a 502 received in time stays a `*StatusError{502}`, `failed`, with no
146	"no answer". `registryFailureReason` returns the error's own text, so the footer
147	(Error) says `Image search on <alias>: no answer within 15 s` and `Could not load
148	tags: no answer within 15 s`, and the journal reads `ERROR [oci_resources] image
149	search on <alias>: no answer within 15 s`. **Limit:** the client's own delay and the
150	context's deadline are still one case: both give the same error and the same text,
151	and `imagesearch.Classify` (DEVDESK-303, IS-12) puts it in the `failed` verdict.
152	Only a delay that satisfies `errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)` becomes a
153	`NoAnswerError`: a transport-level "TLS handshake timeout" keeps its own text. The
154	Docker Hub client of `internal/imagesearch/hub.go` keeps its own 15 s delay,
155	untyped (out of scope).
156	
157	**Credentials stay on their origin (DEVDESK-410).** Four guards keep the Basic
158	credentials and the Bearer token from leaving the registry they were meant for:
159	
160	- **The tag list never follows a `Link: rel="next"` to another origin.**
161	  `ListRegistryTagsContext` checks each `next` with `sameOrigin` (the catalog
162	  walker's guard) before the next request. A foreign `next` is an error that
163	  wraps `ErrTagsNextOffOrigin` (test it with `errors.Is`) and names the
164	  destination host only. No partial list is returned: a short list could pass
165	  for the whole one, and `imageupdate` and the security remediation would read
166	  a false "up to date". The catalog walker behaves otherwise: it returns
167	  `truncated=true` with the names already read, and no error.
168	- **`registryHTTPClient` has a `CheckRedirect`, `RefuseOffOriginRedirect`**
169	  (`internal/oci/guard.go`, exported since DEVDESK-412). A
170	  redirect is refused when its scheme, host or port differ from the first
171	  request of the chain (`via[0]`, not only the previous hop), so a chain that
172	  leaves the origin and comes back is refused too. The error reads
173	  `refusing redirect to another origin (<host>)` and wraps
174	  `ErrOffOriginRedirect` (`errors.Is`). It holds neither the target URL, nor
175	  its path or query: `StripRedirectTarget` strips the `*url.Error` that carries
176	  them, so a signed URL reaches neither the footer nor the logs. The limit of
177	  10 redirects (`MaxRedirects`, the `net/http` default) is kept; past it the
178	  error wraps `ErrTooManyRedirects` (`stopped after 10 redirects`) and no
179	  longer carries the last target URL either. It applies to everything that uses
180	  the client: tags, catalog and the token endpoint.
181	- **The token endpoint's answer is capped at 1 MiB** (`maxTokenResponse`). A
182	  larger body is an error (`token response over 1048576 bytes`), not a silent
183	  cut.
184	- **A Bearer realm on another origin gets no credentials (DEVDESK-629,
185	  D168).** `exchangeBearerTokenContext` calls `checkRealmOrigin`
186	  (`internal/oci/realm.go`) right after `checkTokenRealm`: when credentials
187	  are configured (username and password both set, the condition under which
188	  Basic is sent) and the realm's scheme, host or port differ from the request
189	  that received the challenge, the exchange stops before any request to the
190	  realm with an error wrapping `ErrTokenRealmOffOrigin`
191	  (`token realm on another host (<host>)`, `errors.Is`), naming the realm's host
192	  only and not a `StatusError`. Without credentials the anonymous token request
193	  goes out as before. The comparison is `sameOrigin`'s, exact: `host` and
194	  `host:443` are two origins (H2). Two exceptions, frozen in `realmExceptions`
195	  (a test pins the list), one way, https on both sides, host exact with no
196	  port: Docker Hub (`registry-1.docker.io` to `auth.docker.io`) and GitLab.com
197	  (`registry.gitlab.com` to `gitlab.com`). A self-hosted GitLab registry whose
198	  realm is on the GitLab host is refused. The refusal shows at the footer, level
199	  Error, as `token realm on another host`, in the three interactive flows of the
200	  registry browser: tags opened from the search (`Could not load tags: token

384	  `/v2/_catalog` or to another repository would attach the names of another
385	  catalog to the prefix, so it ends the walk as `truncated`, unfollowed. With
386	  an empty prefix any same-origin path is followed, as before.

396	never carries the prefix or a credential, when it has an empty segment (leading,

399	segment over 255 bytes or a prefix over 1024 bytes. The blank segment, the

404	## Image search — `internal/imagesearch` (DEVDESK-298, IS-18)
405	
406	Pure Go, no UI. Types and one interface; two adapters, `HubSearcher` (IS-02)
407	and `CatalogSearcher` (IS-03); dhi.io is IS-17:
408	
409	- `Target`: one registry to search (`EntryKey`, `Alias`, `RegistryURL`,
410	  `APIURL`, `RepoPrefix`, `Username`, `Password`; the credentials are empty for
411	  an anonymous entry, D12).
412	- `Query{Text, Limit}`: `Limit` 0 is the adapter's default.
413	- `Image`: one result (`EntryKey`, `Name`, `Repo`, `Description`, `Stars`,
414	  `HasStars`, `Official`). `Repo` is the final path, with the prefix and
415	  `library/` applied once (D39).
416	- `Searcher.Search(ctx, Target, Query) (images, partial, err)`, and
417	  `SearcherFunc`, the function adapter.
418	- `HubSearcher` (DEVDESK-301, IS-02, `hub.go`): anonymous, one GET on
419	  `https://index.docker.io/v1/search` (the endpoint `docker search` uses, not a
420	  public Hub contract), one page of at most `HubLimit` (50) results, no
421	  credentials (Target's are ignored), no redirects, 15 s client timeout, body
422	  capped at 1 MiB. A non-200 answer is an `*oci.StatusError`. A result without
423	  `star_count` keeps `HasStars` false (the Stars cell stays empty, never 0).
424	  Names are validated against a regex (`hubComponent`: lowercase alphanumerics
425	  joined by `.`, `_`, `__` or runs of `-`, as in the OCI distribution spec); a
426	  name that fails is dropped (`-rm`, `--help`, uppercase, `a//b`, a leading or
427	  trailing separator). A description is sanitised: escape sequences, control
428	  characters and Unicode format characters (category Cf: bidi overrides,
429	  zero-width, BOM) are removed. Privacy: the text the user typed is sent to
430	  Docker Hub as soon as a Hub entry is checked.
431	- `ByRegistry(hub, other)` (`route.go`): a target whose host is exactly `dhi.io`
432	  (DEVDESK-303, `isDHI`: case, scheme, port and path ignored; `registry.dhi.io`
433	  and `notdhi.io` are not dhi.io) is refused first, with `ErrUnsupported` and no
434	  request to either searcher, since dhi.io has no documented catalogue API
435	  (IS-17). Otherwise a target for which `oci.IsDockerHub(RegistryURL)` is true
436	  goes to `hub`, any other to `other`. A nil searcher answers `ErrUnsupported`
437	  with no request at all. Production uses
438	  `ByRegistry(HubSearcher{}, CatalogSearcher{})`: Hub goes to the Hub search,
439	  every other registry to its catalog. `isDHI` parses the URL (`url.Parse`, with
440	  `https://` added when there is no scheme) and compares `Hostname()`, so
441	  userinfo (`dhi.io@evil.example`), a trailing dot and a port cannot fool it.
442	- `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306, IS-03, `catalog.go`): searches a private
443	  registry by walking `/v2/_catalog` through `oci.ListCatalogContext` (or, for a
444	  Nexus member, `/v2/<prefix>/_catalog`, see "Catalog under a prefix" below) and
445	  filtering **client-side**: the text the user typed is never sent to the
446	  registry. Steps, in order:
447	  1. The query is trimmed; fewer than `CatalogMinQueryRunes` (2) runes returns
448	     `ErrQueryTooShort` with **no request**.
449	  2. The walk: `CatalogPageSize` (1000) names per page, at most
450	     `CatalogMaxPages` (10) pages, so at most 10 000 names. A cut walk sets
451	     `truncated`. An error from the walk (status, deadline, unreadable page)
452	     is returned as is, with no row.
453	  3. Guard R1 (before the filter), **root catalog only**: when the target has a `RepoPrefix`, only the
454	     names that start with `<prefix>/` are candidates. If the walk is complete and
455	     no name carries the prefix, the answer is `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` (the
456	     cause names the prefix); this protects against a catalog that does not
457	     list names the way the entry reaches them (Nexus, IS-16) and would
458	     otherwise read as a false "no result". If the walk is truncated, the
459	     prefix may be on a page not read: the answer is no result with
460	     `partial` set, not an error. A target with `CatalogUnderPrefix` skips this
461	     step (see below).
462	  4. Filter: case-insensitive substring match on the part **after** the prefix.
463	     `Image.Name` is that part, `Image.Repo` the full catalog name.
464	  5. Only valid names are kept (`validRepoPath`, `names.go`: every
465	     `/`-separated component follows the distribution-spec grammar, as for Hub);
466	     others are dropped.
467	  6. Order by `MatchTier`, then name, then `Repo`; at most `CatalogMaxRows`
468	     (100) rows (`Query.Limit` can only lower that). Rows cut by the limit set
469	     `partial`, as does a truncated walk.
470	
471	  `MatchTier` (ranks 0 to 4, see the order below) now lives in `imagesearch`
472	  (`names.go`) so the searcher and the table share one ranking;
473	  `oci_resources.matchTier` delegates to it. The 15 s per-registry deadline
474	  (`imageSearchDeadline`, below) covers the whole walk; hitting it is a
475	  `failed` verdict with no row. `CatalogSearcher.List` replaces
476	  `oci.ListCatalogContext` in tests. Walks per search
477	  (DEVDESK-311, IS-07, `walks.go`): `WithSharedWalks(ctx)` puts a memo on the
478	  batch context and `CatalogSearcher` goes through `walkCatalog`, so a search
479	  queries `/v2/_catalog` once per API URL and identity. Without the memo
480	  (any other caller) every call walks on its own.
481	  - Key: the exact API URL (trailing slash ignored), the catalog prefix
482	    (`catalogPrefix`, empty for the root catalog; DEVDESK-579) and the identity, an
483	    HMAC-SHA256 of username and password under a random per-batch key: no
484	    secret is held in clear and the key prints no userinfo. Two identities
485	    never share a walk, because Harbor, Artifactory and GitLab filter the
486	    catalog per account. A `credentials` entry with no effective secret shares
487	    the walk of an anonymous entry. A member on another port or subdomain has
488	    another API URL and is not grouped. Two Nexus members of one host read two
489	    different catalogs, so they have two keys and two walks: D140 no longer
490	    merges them (D167 amends it). Entries on the root catalog still share one
491	    walk per API URL and identity.
492	  - Leader and followers: the first call for a key walks, the others wait (or
493	    return on their own context). It is a memo, not a singleflight: the key is
494	    kept after the walk, so a member arriving later reuses the result, and it
495	    dies with the batch (no cache between two searches).
496	  - A shared failure (a 503, say) is the same error for every member, so the
497	    same verdict (`failed` or `refused`), one message per entry. A result
498	    caused by the leader's own context ending is not memoized: followers
499	    already waiting on that flight receive the leader's context error (verdict
500	    `failed`), and only members arriving afterwards walk again. A
501	    panic in the leader gives followers a sentinel error (`errWalkAborted`),
502	    never an empty catalog.
503	  - `repo_prefix` filtering, `partial`, `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` and the
504	    `May omit images` mention stay computed per member.
505	  - Members of one Nexus host do **not** answer on the same `/v2/_catalog`
506	    (measured, Nexus 3.98.1-01): each answers on its own path catalog, which is why
507	    the key carries the prefix. For other registries on one host the assumption
508	    stays unverified.
509	  A catalog may be disabled or filtered to the account's rights (Harbor,
510	  Artifactory, GitLab): the answer is then `refused` or a shortened list.
511	- **`Target.CatalogUnderPrefix` (DEVDESK-579, NX-12).** A Nexus member has no
512	  usable root catalog: `/v2/_catalog` answers 404 on the HTTP port, and on a
513	  group connector it lists the members' names together with no member attribution.
514	  With the flag set, `CatalogSearcher` hands the lister `catalogPrefix = RepoPrefix`
515	  and reads `/v2/<prefix>/_catalog`. Differences from the root catalog:
516	  - Nexus returns names **without** the prefix; `Image.Repo` is rebuilt as
517	    `<prefix>/<name>`.
518	  - No guard R1: every name belongs to the member. An empty catalog is
519	    `no result`, not `refused`.
520	  - A prefix that fails `validRepoPath` is `refused` before any request. That
521	    check refuses uppercase, so a catalog name outside the OCI grammar is
522	    ignored and a member whose repository name has uppercase is refused. Not
523	    measured: whether Nexus serves `/v2/<UpperCaseName>/_catalog`.
524	  - Verdicts: 404, 401, 403 and 405 are `refused`; 5xx, 429 and network errors
525	    are `failed`.
526	  - The walk key holds the prefix (D140 amended, above). No request goes to
527	    `/v2/_catalog` for these targets.
528	  Who sets the flag is the UI's decision: see "Image search and Nexus members"
529	  below. Every other target keeps the root catalog and R1.
530	- **Verdicts (DEVDESK-303, IS-12, `verdict.go`).** `Classify(err, n, partial)`
531	  is a pure function that turns one registry's answer into an `Outcome{Verdict,
532	  Partial, Skipped}`. `Verdict` is one of `VerdictOK` (`ok`), `VerdictNoResult`
533	  (`no result`), `VerdictRefused` (`unsupported or refused`) and
534	  `VerdictFailed` (`failed`); the zero value is not a verdict (`pending`) and
535	  `Classify` never returns it. `Partial` and `Skipped` are marks, not verdicts:
536	  `Partial` with `ok` or `no result` (invariant Q1: a walk cut short that found
537	  nothing is still `no result`, marked `Partial`), never with `refused` or
538	  `failed`, never with `Skipped`; `Skipped` only with `no result`. Rules, first
539	  match wins:
540	  1. no error: `n > 0` is `ok`, `n == 0` is `no result`; `Partial` is kept as
541	     given in both cases;
542	  2. `ErrQueryTooShort` is `no result` with `Skipped`;
543	  3. `ErrUnsupported` or `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` is `refused`;
544	  4. a `*oci.StatusError` is `refused` when `refusedStatus` holds: 401 and 403
545	     from either source, 404 and 405 from `SourceRegistry` only (a 404 from the
546	     token endpoint is a failure), except a 404 marked `UpstreamBlocked()` (a
547	     Nexus proxy whose upstream is blocked, DEVDESK-632), which is `failed`;
548	     any other status, 429 and 5xx included, is `failed`;
549	  5. anything else is `failed`: deadline, cancel, network, unreadable or
550	     oversized body, invalid request.
551	
552	  `ErrQueryTooShort` and `ErrPrefixNotInCatalog` are returned by
553	  `CatalogSearcher` (DEVDESK-306).

766	`targetFor(entry)` (same credentials as the tag flow, `credsFor`). Each command
767	wraps the lot's context in `context.WithTimeout(ctx, imageSearchDeadline)`:

769	of the 15 s client timeout per request (`imageSearchDeadline = oci.RequestTimeout`,

783	**Image search and Nexus members (DEVDESK-579, NX-12).** `targetFor` sets
784	`CatalogUnderPrefix` on two kinds of entry: a plain entry that lists cached
785	content only and has a `repo_prefix` (a `parent:` entry of a `provider: nexus`
786	group), and a discovered member of a Nexus group that has a `repo_prefix`. The two
787	tests are equivalent, because `checkRepoPrefixes` refuses a `repo_prefix` on a
788	group. Any other entry keeps the root catalog and guard R1.

790	`searchUnits` decides what a lot searches. Discovered members **without an
791	address of their own** (same URL and same `repo_prefix` as their group, with the
792	group's slug as `ParentSlug`) are merged into **one** unit, the group, labelled
793	`<alias> (group)` (`groupUnitSuffix`). It is walked once, and its rows name no
794	member: Nexus does not say which member holds a name. By design this bypasses the
795	picker's selection: ticking one bare member searches the whole group, and a row can
796	carry the name of a member that was unticked. A group that was not discovered (a
797	pull account) is searched as itself, with its bare label. The Registry column
798	keeps the whole suffix when it cuts a cell (`datatable.Column.KeepSuffix`, see
799	`ui-components.md`). `lotUnits` holds the units of the current lot until the next

805	(`browser_summary.go`, called from `GetHeaderInfo`) says what the lot did, one

810	query is shorter than `imagesearch.CatalogMinQueryRunes`). A class with nothing
811	to say has no line, so a lot where every registry answered shows only `Images`.
812	`summarizeSearch` (pure) sorts the lot's keys into the classes. A name is the
813	Registry column's label (`entryLabel`: alias, else URL, else key), in form order.
814	`Partial` lists registries cut at a cap, `No result` those that answered with
815	nothing (Skipped excluded). A registry that is both partial and empty appears
816	on both lines, on purpose.

819	they hold, by their role in a Nexus group (DEVDESK-629, F2; it replaces the

831	what a member it could not reach left out), a proxy only when it `failed` or was

101:**D168 — DEVDESK-629 (F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, F8): Nexus corrections from NX-04 and NX-05; point 1 (token realm policy) is implemented by DEVDESK-630. Decided (user, story DEVDESK-629, 2026-11-20; plan `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-629-plan.md`). (1) **A Bearer realm off the origin is never followed with credentials.** The token exchange (`exchangeBearerTokenContext`, the only such site in the product) refuses, before any request, a realm whose scheme, host or port differ from the request that received the challenge, **when credentials are configured** (username and password both set, the condition under which Basic is sent); without credentials the anonymous token request goes out as before. Typed error `oci.ErrTokenRealmOffOrigin` (`token realm on another host (<host>)`, test with `errors.Is`), naming the realm's host only, never its userinfo, path or query; not a `StatusError`. The origin is compared as `sameOrigin` does (exact scheme and `u.Host`): `host` and `host:443` differ, `http` and `https` differ (refuse when in doubt, as D156). Two frozen exceptions (`realmExceptions` in `internal/oci/realm.go`, pinned by `TestRealmExceptionsAreFrozen`), one way only (registry to realm), https on both sides, host compared exactly with no port: Docker Hub (`registry-1.docker.io` to `auth.docker.io`) and **GitLab.com (`registry.gitlab.com` to `gitlab.com`, whose registry names `https://gitlab.com/jwt/auth` as its realm)**. A self-hosted GitLab registry whose realm is on the GitLab host stays refused: a per-configuration exception is a follow-up story. Rejected: following the realm with the credentials removed (an anonymous token is useless to an authenticated caller and would hide the refusal); an exception per configuration (follow-up). Reason: the `X-Forwarded-Host` probe of NX-05 shows that a Nexus behind a reverse proxy announces the host it is told, so a realm is not trustworthy by itself. Display: footer, level Error, `token realm on another host` (tags opened from the search, tags opened from the form, which used to be silent, and image search); verdict `failed` in the search. Other callers (`imageupdate`, signature, remediation) have no footer: journal and column unchanged. Amends D156 (the guards stopped at the scheme of the realm) and the pin of `TestMeasuredRealmStaysOnTheRegistryOrigin` (the frozen note `docs/measurements/2026-11-20-nexus-access.md` describes the code before this change and is not edited). (2) The 404 `Remote Auto Blocked` of a proxy whose upstream is cut is `failed`, temporary, detected on the JSON `message` with a body read up to 4 KiB (step 3). Implemented by DEVDESK-632: `registryStatusError(resp)` (`internal/oci/status_body.go`) reads the body only on a 404 and marks the `*oci.StatusError` (`UpstreamBlocked()`) when `errors[0].message` starts with `Remote Auto Blocked`, exact and case-sensitive; any other 404 stays `refused`, and a body read that ends on a deadline is a `*NoAnswerError` (`failed`), not a 404; `ManifestDigest` is a HEAD without a body, so a `Remote Auto Blocked` 404 on a manifest is never marked and stays a plain 404; the error reads `registry returned 404: the proxy's upstream is temporarily blocked, try again later`, never the body, date or duration; footer `Could not load tags: the proxy's upstream is temporarily blocked`. (3) The timeout message reads `no answer within 15 s` from `oci.RequestTimeout`, delay unchanged (step 4). Implemented by DEVDESK-633: `*oci.NoAnswerError` (`internal/oci/noanswer.go`) wraps only `context.DeadlineExceeded`, so no URL, userinfo, host or query reaches the message; it is applied to the request, token and body-read errors of the registry client, `context.Canceled` is untouched, a timely 502 stays a `*StatusError`, the verdict stays `failed`, and `registryFailureReason` shows it at the footer and in the journal. Only a delay that satisfies `errors.Is(context.DeadlineExceeded)` becomes a `NoAnswerError` (a transport "TLS handshake timeout" keeps its text); the Docker Hub client of `internal/imagesearch/hub.go` keeps its own untyped 15 s delay (out of scope). (4) Docker credentials of an entry with a path: exact key, then `host[:port]` as written (step 6); the port is kept as written, never normalized, and an `anonymous` entry still sends nothing; logout stays on the exact key (DEVDESK-635); review fix M1: when `management_url` names another host than the registry URL, the discovery sends that host only a login stored for it (anonymous otherwise), never the registry host's login that the host key now finds; known risk left as is by the user's decision (B1): a login stored for `h` or `https://h` also serves `http://h/path`, a clear Basic over http, a prior defect for a URL without a path that the host key extends to a URL with one, a separate story may refuse Basic over http outside loopback. 37	Like `provider`, how a repository is addressed is **declared, never
38	sniffed**. Whether a repository manager exposes a member on a path prefix, a
39	dedicated port, or a subdomain is a setting on that repository, and the one
40	API endpoint that would reveal it typically answers `403` to an ordinary
41	pull account — the same endpoint that would say what a group's members even
42	are. An instance that refuses to answer refuses both questions at once, so
43	guessing at the shape isn't a fallback; it's the failure mode this design
44	avoids.
45	
46	A few consequences follow from treating the prefix as part of the address:
47	
48	- **The prefix is applied exactly once**, at search time, and becomes part
49	  of the resolved repository name from then on — nothing downstream needs
50	  to know about it separately, which would otherwise be two places free to
51	  drift apart.
52	- **A group itself may not declare a prefix.** A group is only reachable
53	  through its own connector; applying a path-prefix trick to a group's own
54	  address the way it's applied to a member just produces a `404`.
55	- **A URL no longer uniquely identifies an entry**, now that several
56	  entries can share one host. Anything that used to key on URL — resolving
57	  a search result back to its entry, tracking which rows are selected in
58	  the browser — now keys on the entry itself (or `(group, member)` for a
59	  discovered member), so two entries on the same host stay independent.
60	
61	The Nexus detector no longer synthesizes an address at all: for a group
62	reached as a path prefix, it reports each member as `(host, memberName)`
63	directly rather than trying to build a browsable-but-unpullable shortcut.
64	For a group reached through its own connector, it reports the group's URL
65	with **no** prefix, because which connector a given member answers on is
66	precisely the thing the detector cannot know from the outside — an empty
67	prefix against a bare host fails visibly, where a guessed path used to fail
68	in a way that looked like it might be working.
69	
70	The Nexus detector does not follow a redirect to another host, so your account
71	is never sent to a server you did not configure. That includes a redirect from
72	`http` to `https` on the same host: enter the registry URL with `https`. When a
73	redirect is refused, discovery finds no members and says so in the log.
74	
75	## Searching images in a Nexus group
76	
77	The image search reads the catalog of a Nexus member on the member's own path,
78	so each member answers for itself. When Nexus lists the members of a group,
79	DevDesk searches the group once and labels it `<alias> (group)`: Nexus does not
80	say which member holds each image, so the results do not name one. Ticking a
81	single member in the registry browser still searches the whole group, and a
82	result can come from a member you did not tick.
83	
84	Two limits to know. A repository name with an uppercase letter cannot be
85	searched this way; DevDesk refuses it without sending a request. And a Nexus
86	account restricted to some repositories may see a shorter catalog, which can
87	show as "no result".
88

I'm checking the remaining Nexus bench notes, including the IS-07 contradiction for hosted members and the IS-14 contradiction, and I'm noting that IS-16 isn't documented. Next I'll make the first edit to the network doc.

Like `provider`, it is **declared, never sniffed**. Whether a repository answers
on a path prefix, a connector port or a subdomain is a setting on that repository
(`docker.httpPort`, `docker.httpsPort`, `docker.subdomain`), and the one endpoint
carrying it answers 403 to an ordinary pull account — the same endpoint that
would say what a group's members are. An instance that refuses one refuses both,
so guessing is not a fallback, it is the defect.

The same declaration drives the image search header (DEVDESK-308, reworded by
- **A Nexus member** (a discovered member of a `provider: nexus` group, or a
  `parent:` entry of one, DEVDESK-579) is read on its own path,
  `/v2/<repo_prefix>/_catalog`. Nexus answers with names that do not carry the
  prefix; DevDesk rebuilds `<repo_prefix>/<name>`. An empty catalog is "no
  result"; a 404, 401, 403 or 405 is refused. One walk per member.
- **Any other entry** walks the root catalog of its host (`/v2/_catalog`), keeps
  the names under `<repo_prefix>/` and matches the typed text on the part after
8:792:company instance: read "Measured Nexus behavior" after this section before
10:869:**Measured Nexus behavior (NX-03, NX-04, NX-05).** Where the code rests on how
11:873:no TLS, file blob store, six repository names, one pull account with rights on
13:887:| Detailed group endpoint (2026-11-17) | `GET /service/rest/v1/repositories/<format>/group/<name>`: the pull account gets **404** `Repository not found`, anonymous gets 403, admin gets `memberNames`. The generic endpoint answers all three, without members | The D161 expectation of a 403 for the pull account: **contradicted** (DEVDESK-578) | the 404 with that exact message is a members refusal (`registries.md`) |

Each name list is fitted by `fitNames` to the room a value has
(`shortcut.HeaderValueWidth`), so the `+N` is never lost: all the names, else
the first k names then `+N`, else `+N` alone. `Skipped` carries the hint
` (type N+ characters)`, which is the first thing dropped when the header is
narrow. The summary has a budget of `shortcut.HeaderRows` (7) lines, `Images`
included; classes after the sixth are left out (with `May omit images` the seven
classes fit only because `Pending`/`Interrupted` and `Skipped`/`May omit images`
exclude each other). Before the first
`WindowSizeMsg` nothing is abbreviated. At level 2 (tags) the header is the
usual tag count.

Limit, accepted (R2): below about 50 columns `HeaderValueWidth` is 0 or 1,
nothing fits, `fitNames` returns `+N` anyway and the router clips it.

Logging, by verdict, through `logSearchOutcome` (the alias falls back to the
entry key):
- `failed`: `ERROR [oci_resources] image search on <alias>: <cause>`;
- `refused`: `INFO [oci_resources] image search on <alias>: unsupported or
  refused: <cause>` (a refusal is expected for dhi.io and for a registry whose catalog
  is disabled, forbidden or not under the entry's prefix, so it does not fill
  the error log);
- `ok` and `no result`: nothing.

The cause is `searchErrorCause(err)`: a `*url.Error` keeps only its Op and Err
(the URL carries the typed text and can carry credentials), then
`jobs.SafeCause`. Nothing else reaches the log. Nothing reaches the screen
either, and no error text reaches `:jobs` (Rule 128).

Level 1 shows `searchTable` (`datatable.Model[searchRow]`, built by
`newSearchTable`, also used by `ActivityTables` as `oci/registry-search`).
Columns: the activity column (`IndicatorColumn`, always `Idle`, `IconDocker` in
the `IconRoleImage` role), Name (flex, searchable), Registry, Stars (empty when
`HasStars` is false), Official (`official` or empty) and Description
(searchable). All cells are plain text (Rule 122). When the terminal narrows,
Description, then Stars, then Official leave whole (`Optional`, with
`DropFirst` on Description and Stars). Stars reserves 7 cells (title plus sort arrow). On Docker Hub rows this makes Description and Stars e

- **A Nexus member** (a discovered member of a `provider: nexus` group, or a
  `parent:` entry of one, DEVDESK-579) is read on its own path,
  `/v2/<repo_prefix>/_catalog`. Nexus (3.98.1-01 Community, measured on the bench
  on 2026-11-17) answers with names that do not carry the
  prefix; DevDesk rebuilds `<repo_prefix>/<name>`. An empty catalog is "no
  result"; a 404, 401, 403 or 405 is refused. One walk per member.
- **Any other entry** walks the root catalog of its host (`/v2/_catalog`), keeps
  the names under `<repo_prefix>/` and matches the typed text on the part after
  it. A catalog with no name under the prefix is refused, not "no result".
  `discovery`, never in place of it (`mcp.md`).
- **Known limits.** Two processes writing the cache at once: the last write
  wins, as before. That Nexus answers 403 on the format endpoint to a pull-only
  account was a hypothesis (D161): the bench answers 404 (below); the 403 seen on a
  company instance on 2026-08-10 is not settled. What stays open: a restricted account, another Nexus version, and
  the company instance, where this was never measured (see "Measured Nexus
  behavior" in `network.md`).
- **Measured on the local bench, Nexus 3.98.1-01 Community, 2026-11-17 (NX-03,
  fixtures of DEVDESK-511).** The pull
  account gets **404 `Repository not found`**, not 403, on the detailed group
  endpoint; the anonymous call gets 403. The 403 of D161 was a hypothesis the
  bench disproved. The 2026-08-10 observation of a 403 came from a company
  instance of unknown version; it was not cross-checked, so whether the
  difference is the version or the privileges is open. Since DEVDESK-578 (NX-07b) that 404 is a refusal like the
  403: a `*MembersRefusedError{Status: 404}` whose `Cause` is the
  `*oci.StatusError`, stored in `refusals` with `status: 404`, shown as
  `denied · <age>`, with declared members (`repo_prefix`) still listed.
  `TestDetectGroupOnMeasuredNexusAnswers` pins it on the recorded answers. Only
  a 404 whose JSON `message` is `Repository not found` (inner quotes and
  surrounding spaces removed, case ignored) is requalified; any other 404 (empty
  or HTML body, another JSON, a body over 4 KiB, a 404 on the generic
  `/v1/repositories/<name>` endpoint) stays a failed discovery. **Known limit:**
  Nexus sends the same body for a group that does not exist. If the group is

Like `provider`, how a repository is addressed is **declared, never
sniffed**. Whether a repository manager exposes a member on a path prefix, a
dedicated port, or a subdomain is a setting on that repository, and the one
API endpoint that would reveal it typically answers `403` (or `404`, on Nexus 3.98.1) to an ordinary pull account — the same endpoint that would say what a group's members even
are. An instance that refuses to answer refuses both questions at once, so
guessing at the shape isn't a fallback; it's the failure mode this design
avoids.
